messages:
support-esc: heads up — acme-corp opened a support case: their signed webhook callbacks started failing with 401s after their IdP rotated keys earlier today. logs show 'kid not found' and 'signature algorithm mismatch'. repro + basics below.

support-esc: repro: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <jwt>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hooks/acme/callback -> 401. excerpt from our verifier logs:
```
ERROR verifier: signature verification failed: kid "bGdF3x" not found in cached jwks
WARN verifier: jwt header alg PS256 does not match jwk alg RS256 for kid bGdF3x
```

ivan: can you paste the decoded JWT header (no PII except kid/alg) and the jwks keys we still have cached? also what is our jwks cache TTL on the edge that handled this?

support-esc: header (redacted): {
  "alg": "PS256",
  "kid": "bGdF3x",
  "typ": "JWT"
}
cached jwks (from node A): key(id: bGdF3x, alg: RS256, use: sig) — looks like the idp rotated to PS256 but one of our cache nodes still has the old key entry. cache ttl is 10m currently.

sara: my hunch: idp rotated signing algorithm + keyset simultaneously. some of our nodes refreshed their JWKS and got the new PS256 key, others still have the old RS256 entry mapped to the same kid (or the kid reused). verifier code currently rejects if jwk.alg != header.alg — correct but causes hard failure if jwks are inconsistent across nodes.

mike: quick mitigation: on kid-not-found OR alg-mismatch, immediately fetch the jwks endpoint once (bypass cache) and retry verification exactly once. pseudocode:
```
verify(jwt):
  header = decodeHeader(jwt)
  jwk = cache.lookup(header.kid)
  if !jwk or jwk.alg != header.alg:
    jwks = fetchJwks(remoteUrl) // bypass cache
    cache.replace(remoteUrl, jwks)
    jwk = jwks.find(k => k.kid == header.kid)
    if jwk and jwk.alg == header.alg:
      return verifyWithKey(jwt, jwk)
    else:
      return 401
  else:
    return verifyWithKey(jwt, jwk)
```

eng-infra-oncall: note: if we flip to fetch-on-miss we need to rate-limit and circuit-break to avoid being throttled by aggressive retries (esp. during mass rotation). we should emit metrics: jwks_fetch_on_miss_count, jwks_fetch_fail_rate, jwk_mismatch_count. tagging @mike @ivan to own instrumentation.

security-bot: alert: JWKS fetch error rate spiked 2024-05-01T14:22Z -> https://internal.redwood/alerts/ALERT-7901 (auto).

ivan: additional short-term mitigations: (1) reduce jwks cache TTL to 30s on the edge for public IdP endpoints that rotate frequently, (2) implement the fetch-on-miss+single-retry above, (3) keep tightened logs to capture header and matched jwk metadata for postmortem. i'll open a ticket.

support-esc: opened INC-2026 and created github issue gh#1468: "JWKS: retry fetch on kid-miss/alg-mismatch + rate-limited refresh shim". assigned to @ivan and @mike. customer notified that we're working on a rollback/mitigation.

mike: also consider a small clock skew/iat leeway (5s) for time-related failures — but that won't help alg mismatches. example in verifier conf: allowClockSkewSeconds: 5.

sara: agreed — leeway only helps exp/iat. alg/key mismatch requires either coordinated key rotation or a smoother key transition strategy (dual-signing window or key reuse avoidance). ask IdP to publish rotation schedule / reuse policy.

eng-infra-oncall: i'll add a rate-limited fetch shim (max 1 fetch/s with token bucket across the fleet) and expose metrics. will also add a per-tenant override TTL flag we can toggle from ops for emergencies.

support-esc: thanks all — updating customer. next steps: implement fetch-on-miss + rate-limiter, shorten TTL for this IdP, capture additional logs, and follow up in INC-2026. will post timeline here once we have PR and rollout plan. :thumbsup:
